name: MMStar
description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 challenging samples meticulously selected by humans to evaluate large vision-language models' multi-modal capacities. MMStar covers 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, with carefully balanced and purified samples designed to ensure visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and advanced multi-modal capability requirements.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2, 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MMStar samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline, then strict manual review and selection are applied to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples. The source benchmarks are MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista. The curation criteria are: visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and requiring advanced multi-modal capabilities for resolution. The automated filtering uses eight LLM inspectors to evaluate whether samples can be answered without visual input; samples with more than two hits are excluded. After coarse filtering, three experts manually review samples to ensure visual dependency, coverage of capability dimensions, and advanced multimodal difficulty, while considering diversity and difficulty levels.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source is existing multi-modal benchmarks: MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista. The paper states they began with a total of 22,401 samples from these benchmarks, reduced to 11,607 candidate samples after coarse filtering, and finally selected 1,500 samples for MMStar.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLM inspectors were excluded as they may have leakage or visual-unnecessary problems. The remaining coarsely filtered samples were evaluated by 16 LVLMs and split into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Final manual curation considered both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied to samples from six existing benchmarks. Two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs of size 20B or larger served as inspectors. The open-source LLMs were applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting. Hit frequency was documented for each sample, and only samples with hit counts of two or fewer were retained. This reduced the sample pool from 22,401 to 11,607 before manual review.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review of coarsely filtered samples to ensure that each sample's answer should be based on understanding visual content, selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions, and most samples require advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. The final benchmark is organized into 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, with each core capability containing 250 samples.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To expedite manual selection of samples with varying difficulty levels, the authors tallied the hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Final selection considered both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo and GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (including Qwen-1.5-72B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B, Mixtral-8x7B, and LLaMA2-70B) were used as inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage. Sixteen LVLMs were used to gauge sample difficulty. Experiments were conducted in a codebase modified from VLMEvalKit.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that in the future, they plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper argues that inappropriate questions and data leakage can lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLMs. It states that for research to be transparent and equitable, it is imperative to account for and mitigate such leakage so that models are evaluated on their true ability to integrate and interpret multi-modal data rather than memorize specific samples.
rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies two benchmark biases/issues in existing multimodal evaluations: many samples do not require visual content and can be answered from text-only world knowledge or question wording, and unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training. These issues can unfairly inflate benchmark performance and distort comparisons.
rai:dataLimitations: Even on MMStar, the best evaluated model scores under 60 on average. The paper also notes future plans to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods, implying the current benchmark is limited in size and static. The benchmark is constructed from existing benchmarks and aims to minimize, rather than guarantee elimination of, accidental data leakage.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is intended for evaluating large vision-language models' multi-modal capabilities, benchmarking 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, and assessing visual dependency, data leakage, and actual multi-modal performance gain. It is used for evaluation/testing rather than training, and the paper evaluates 16 leading LVLMs on MMStar and on 7 benchmarks with the proposed MG and ML metrics.
